html:
SMTO-EXE-0052 — SMTO can't do that desktop action on this computer right now

GUID: 97669668-4953-5c91-b041-345ba37aa372
Slug: desktop-unavailable
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: desktop

What happened

  • The Gateway computer either doesn't support this kind of window or app action, or is already busy with as many desktop actions as it allows. This doesn't always mean something is missing.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait for SMTO's other window or app actions on that computer to finish, then ask again. The Gateway only runs a limited number of desktop actions, and launched apps, at the same time.
  2. If the Gateway computer runs Linux, sign in with an X11 (Xorg) session instead of Wayland; many login screens offer this choice. SMTO's window control on Linux works only in X11 sessions.
  3. If one window refuses a specific action, such as maximize or close, do that step by hand or try another window. Some windows don't offer every control, so that action can't be done on them.
  4. Ask the person who manages the Gateway computer to confirm its desktop support is fully installed, then select Check connection in Settings › Setup › Gateways. Missing system components make desktop actions unavailable until they are added.

What success looks like

  • SMTO can list windows on that computer and the requested action completes.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway computer, saying whether it runs Windows, macOS or Linux. Check the window before asking again if part of the action might have happened.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway's Desktop service could not run the action: no supported native backend or action (e.g. Wayland, missing EWMH/Xlib or pyobjc, absent AX button, DPI context failure) or its 32-operation / 128-launched-app capacity was reached.

What this means

  • The desktop family lacks a supported backend/action or display facility, or its active-operation/owned-child bound was reached. This shared category does not always mean missing installation. These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.

Why this can happen

  • The desktop family lacks a supported backend/action or display facility, or its active-operation/owned-child bound was reached. This shared category does not always mean missing installation.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect desktop.summary and retained failure context for platform support, window-manager/DPI facilities, missing native action or capacity.

How to fix it

  • Run desktop.summary on the Gateway and read backend and unavailable_reason (e.g. wayland-unsupported, headless), then refresh Gateway capabilities. Install the native backend for the platform (python-xlib with an EWMH window manager under X11, pyobjc on macOS) or let active Desktop operations and launched children settle before a new request; never auto-replay an action whose effect is uncertain.
  • Inspect the specific readiness or capacity reason. Restore the supported native prerequisite or let owned work settle before a new request.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect desktop.summary and refresh Gateway capabilities. Install the documented native backend for the desired family.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended family reports ready and admits the operation within its existing bounds.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass identity protection or automatically replay an uncertain mutation.

Technical notes

  • These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
